This is a bit of a guess but it looks like from your other comments that you are using an Nvidia graphics card. Did you install drivers for your graphics card? You can look here for how to do so https://wiki.debian.org/NvidiaGraphicsDrivers .

Basically, for installing Nvidia drivers for a recent graphics card, you'll need to update your /etc/apt/sources.list to allow installing "non-free" packages (not non-free as costs money, but non-free as doesn't agree with Debian's policy of free software). Type sudo nano /etc/apt/sources.list to open an editor "nano" for that file. The first line in that file may be 

deb http://deb.debian.org/debian stretch main

You need to add two words at the end to make it look like

deb http://deb/debian.org/debian stretch main contrib non-free

Then to install the graphics drivers:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install nvidia-driver

I think this may be the problem of why your laptop isn't behaving well but it's a guess, though if you are using an Nvidia graphics card, you would naturally need drivers installed for it.
